expectations.text: Applies top-down scoping: significant accounts/disclosures → business processes → applications that initiate/record/process/report, consistent with AS 2201's risk-based approach
expectations.evidence: "standard top-down, risk-based approach"; "begin with... which financial statement line items are material... trace back to the applications that support them" (COSO/PCAOB cited)

expectations.text: Scopes the named systems sensibly: NetSuite (GL) and the billing engine (revenue) clearly in; Workday in for payroll-to-GL; the data warehouse in because finance relies on its revenue reports (IPE)
expectations.evidence: NetSuite "almost certainly in scope... system of record for the general ledger"; billing "directly drives revenue recognition"; Workday in for payroll expense; warehouse in "if numbers flow from it into the financial statements"

expectations.text: Extends to supporting layers: database, OS/platform, and the access/change/operations ITGC processes for each in-scope application
expectations.evidence: "Underlying infrastructure: databases, servers/cloud hosting... pulled into scope"; ITGC domains "(a) access to programs and data, (b) program changes, (c) program development, (d) computer operations"

expectations.text: Handles outsourced layers via SOC 1 Type II reports: period coverage vs fiscal year, bridge letters for gaps, and mapping CUECs into the company's own control set
expectations.evidence: SOC 1 Type II, "(bridge letter included)" and CUEC mapping mentioned, but no discussion of report-period coverage vs the fiscal year / gap mechanics that bridge letters address

expectations.text: Covers IPE/EUC: reports used in controls need accuracy/completeness validation, and control-relevant spreadsheets enter scope
expectations.evidence: "key spreadsheets used in the close process" pull the warehouse in scope; "particularly for completeness and accuracy of the ETL/transformation logic"
